cues.zh: 从逻辑上看，这完全讲得通。你不可能

cues.en: without the request.
cues.zh: 没有请求就去处理。

cues.en: Well, you can't process the request without this ID. Why would you think you could? Seems perfectly reasonable to make this required.
cues.zh: 好吧，没有这个 ID 你就没法处理请求。你怎么可能处理得了？把这设为 required 看起来合情合理。

cues.en: But what happens when time creeps in? We change the service to have a different option. What if you provide the raw string instead of a pre computed query ID?
cues.zh: 但当时间推移时会发生什么？我们修改了服务，提供了另一种选项。要是传的不是预先计算好的 query ID，而是原始字符串呢？

cues.en: In that case, we aren't sure which one of these will be present, and so maybe we make both the ID or the string optional, and we do the validation at a higher level.
cues.zh: 那种情况下，我们不确定具体会出现哪一个，所以也许我们会把 ID 和字符串都设为 optional，把校验挪到更高层去做。

cues.en: What's that look like when we deploy? We have some front end that is sending requests to the back end server.
cues.zh: 部署的时候会是什么样？我们有一个前端正在向后端服务器发送请求。

cues.en: Unshockingly,
cues.zh: 不出所料，

cues.en: if we deploy the front end first, we'll start sending maybe request ID or maybe sending request string.
cues.zh: 如果我们先部署前端，就会开始发送请求 ID，或者发送请求字符串。

cues.en: And the server, remember,
cues.zh: 而服务器，记住，

cues.en: is somewhere back in time. It is still running with the old definition.
cues.zh: 还停留在过去某个时间点。它仍然按旧定义运行。

cues.en: In the server's view of things, the ID is still required.
cues.zh: 在服务器看来，ID 仍然是必需的。

cues.en: And so if the server is configured so that that garbage request is an assertion failure or just silently ignored,
cues.zh: 所以，如果服务器被配置成把那个无效请求当作断言失败，或者只是静默忽略它，

cues.en: things go sideways.
cues.zh: 事情就出岔子了。

cues.en: None of this is surprising, right? We update the server first, this is very in line with everything that everyone knows about writing protocols.
cues.zh: 这些都不意外，对吧？我们先更新服务器，这非常符合大家对编写协议的共识。

cues.en: You need to be strict in what you omit and liberal in what you accept, so clearly we have to update the backend first.
cues.zh: 你发送时要严格，接收时要宽容，所以显然必须先更新后端。

cues.en: No shock.
cues.zh: 毫不意外。

cues.en: Make sure we're capable of accepting any definition.
cues.zh: 确保我们能够接受任何定义。

cues.en: But what about rollouts? What if there are multiple servers? What if we don't upgrade all the servers at once? That does seem safest after all. We know the previous version was working.
cues.zh: 但分批发布呢？如果有多个服务器呢？如果我们不一次性升级所有服务器呢？毕竟那看起来最安全。我们知道上一个版本是能正常工作的。

cues.en: Updating all the servers to the new version at once might be catastrophic.
cues.zh: 一次把所有服务器都升级到新版本，可能是灾难性的。

cues.en: So we do some of them, and then the front end, and if the front end doesn't know the difference between which ones support the new thing and which ones don't, then we're back to the same problem.
cues.zh: 所以我们先升级一部分，再更新前端；如果前端分不清哪些服务器支持新功能、哪些不支持，那我们就又回到同样的问题了。

cues.en: This only gets worse when you start having complex networks of servers.
cues.zh: 当你开始面对复杂的服务器网络时，这只会更糟。

cues.en: I could not possibly draw the graph of server interconnects in Google production.
cues.zh: 我根本不可能画出 Google 生产环境中服务器互连的图。

cues.en: Right? You do not want to get into a situation where every service in the fleet has to be restarted all at once in order to handle a protocol update.
cues.zh: 对吧？你绝不希望陷入这样一种局面：为了处理一次协议更新，整个集群里的每个服务都必须同时重启。

cues.en: And so, we could of course fix this by adding version fields to every message definition,
cues.zh: 当然，我们可以通过给每个消息定义加上版本字段来解决这个问题，

cues.en: but that in and of itself is still adding time to the protocol.
cues.zh: 但这本身仍然是在给协议增加时间维度。

cues.en: All of this complexity is fundamentally a different flavor than I got it working.
cues.zh: 所有这些复杂性，本质上和“我把它跑通了”是两回事。

cues.en: It is fundamentally a different flavor than programming.
cues.zh: 它本质上和编程是两回事。

cues.en: And it is completely unnecessary in some contexts.
cues.zh: 而且在某些场景下，它完全没有必要。

cues.en: If you know that your program or service only needs to work for a limited time, right? I need to get it today, I need it to last through the demo, I need the next round of funding, we don't need to plan for the future,
cues.zh: 如果你知道你的程序或服务只需要运行有限的时间，对吧？我今天就得把它搞定，我得让它撑过演示，我得拿到下一轮融资，我们不需要为未来做规划，

cues.en: then you don't plan for the future.
cues.zh: 那你就不用为未来做规划。

cues.en: That's fine.
cues.zh: 这没问题。

cues.en: Right? Context matters.
cues.zh: 对吧？情境很重要。

cues.en: But when you aren't certain, when you have to be prepared, and that preparedness
cues.zh: 但当你并不确定，当你必须做好准备，而这种准备

cues.en: is what I look at as software engineering.
cues.zh: 正是我所理解的软件工程。

cues.en: It is the impact of time on a programming system.
cues.zh: 它是时间对编程系统的影响。

cues.en: And the point of this whole anecdote is that something that makes sense on the face of it,
cues.zh: 而整个这段轶事的重点是：有些东西表面上看起来合理，

cues.en: required fields,
cues.zh: 必填字段，

cues.en: turns out to be a horrible idea when you start thinking about change over time.
cues.zh: 当你开始考虑随时间发生的变化时，却会变成糟糕的主意。

cues.en: And I would argue that there are many things that we do
cues.zh: 而且我认为，我们做的很多事情

cues.en: that make perfect sense
cues.zh: 完全说得通

cues.en: in a limited domain, in a programming domain, but do not necessarily make sense when we are thinking about it as engineering
cues.zh: 在有限的领域、在编程领域里，但当我们把它当作工程来思考时，就未必说得通

cues.en: and change over time.
cues.zh: 以及考虑随时间变化时。

cues.en: At the core, I think everything that we think of when we talk about software engineering tools and technology is about resilience to time.
cues.zh: 本质上，我们谈到软件工程工具和技术时想到的一切，都关乎对时间的韧性。

cues.en: Version control is about being able to go back in time.
cues.zh: 版本控制就是能回到过去。

cues.en: Coordinate with your colleagues over time.
cues.zh: 与同事跨时间协作。

cues.en: CI, continuous integration, is about making sure that recent changes haven't broken the system.
cues.zh: 持续集成（CI）就是确保最近的改动没有破坏系统。

cues.en: Unit tests are very similar. This is make sure the feature that you wrote hasn't been broken by the idiot down the hall, or you in the future.
cues.zh: 单元测试也很像。它确保你写的功能没被走廊那头的蠢货，或者未来的你弄坏。

cues.en: Refactoring tools are how you update from an old way to a new way.
cues.zh: 重构工具让你从旧方式更新到新方式。

cues.en: Design patterns give you some ability to plan for future changes without knowing exactly what those changes will be.
cues.zh: 设计模式让你能在不完全知道未来变化是什么的情况下，为未来变化做些规划。

cues.en: Dependency management is how we deal with the fact that the libraries we depend upon may change.
cues.zh: 依赖管理处理的是我们所依赖的库可能会变化这一事实。

cues.en: And that last is really crucial and what I'm gonna talk about for a while here. Let's talk about dependency management and the fundamental problem in dependency management,
cues.zh: 最后这一点非常关键，也是我要在这里讲一会儿的内容。我们来谈谈依赖管理，以及依赖管理中的根本问题，

cues.en: Diamond dependencies.
cues.zh: 菱形依赖。

cues.en: Diamond dependencies are the bane of package management, content management, dependency management, any sort of management.
cues.zh: 菱形依赖是包管理、内容管理、依赖管理，乃至各种管理的祸根。

cues.en: And they arise commonly in cases where multiple libraries depend on a lower level library.
cues.zh: 它们常见于多个库依赖同一个底层库的情况。

cues.en: Here we have libA and libB. They both depend on libUtil.
cues.zh: 这里有 libA 和 libB。它们都依赖 libUtil。

cues.en: As soon as versions change, there's now two green boxes for libUtil.
cues.zh: 一旦版本变化，libUtil 现在就变成两个绿框。

cues.en: If everyone in your infrastructure doesn't upgrade at the same time,
cues.zh: 如果你的基础设施中所有人不是同时升级，

cues.en: then we have version skew.
cues.zh: 就会产生版本偏差。

cues.en: Lib B depends on V two, Lib A depends on V one.
cues.zh: Lib B 依赖 V2，Lib A 依赖 V1。

cues.en: This is even now still fine in theory, until some additional package, maybe yours,
cues.zh: 理论上即便如此也仍然没问题，直到某个额外的包，也许是你的包，

cues.en: chooses to depend on both of the mid level libraries.
cues.zh: 选择同时依赖这两个中间层库。

cues.en: Now, we have a problem. You are the pink box.
cues.zh: 现在，问题来了。你就是那个粉色方框。

cues.en: In some situations,
cues.zh: 在某些情况下，

cues.en: for some languages,
cues.zh: 对某些语言而言，

cues.en: we can make this work by compiling in both versions of libutil.
cues.zh: 我们可以通过同时编译两个版本的 libutil 来让它工作。

cues.en: So long as there are not types from libutil that pass through both of them into user code, and so long as there's not global initialization in libutil,
cues.zh: 只要没有来自 libutil 的类型经由这两个库传入用户代码，并且只要 libutil 中没有全局初始化，

cues.en: and a long host of other things. But in general, for many languages and for many situations, this just results in failed builds. Or maybe in some cases worse, failed runtime problems.
cues.zh: 以及一长串其他条件。但总体来说，对很多语言和很多场景，这只会导致构建失败。有时甚至更糟，导致运行时故障。

cues.en: There is a standard mechanism that we use for identifying this problem. And it is so ubiquitous,
cues.zh: 我们有一种标准机制用来识别这个问题。而且它如此普遍，

cues.en: it's even worked its way into this diagram. When discussing two incompatible versions of Libutil,
cues.zh: 甚至已经融入了这张图。在讨论 libUtil 的两个不兼容版本时，

cues.en: my instinct is to describe these as versions one and version two.
cues.zh: 我的本能是把它们称为版本一和版本二。

cues.en: Not one and one point o one. Not apple and orange. Not a and b. Clearly, I describe these as one and two.
cues.zh: 不是 1 和 1.0.1。不是苹果和橙子。不是 A 和 B。显然，我会把它们说成一和二。

cues.en: This is what was intuitive to you as well, I'll guess.
cues.zh: 我猜这对你来说也很直观。

cues.en: We've come to take it for granted that version numbers are what identifies a release,
cues.zh: 我们已习以为常地认为版本号标识一个发布版本，

cues.en: and changes in major version indicate some level of incompatibility.
cues.zh: 而主版本号变化表示某种程度的不兼容。

cues.en: You changed a thing. This is what we call semantic versioning, and it is the standard answer for versioning and dependency management.
cues.zh: 你改了一个东西。这就是我们所说的语义化版本控制，它是版本管理和依赖管理的标准答案。

cues.en: Semantic versioning, just so that we're all on the same page, generally gives us version numbers of the form X dot Y dot Z,
cues.zh: 语义化版本控制，先对齐一下概念，通常给出的版本号形式是 X.Y.Z，

cues.en: one dot three dot 17 for instance.
The
cues.zh: 最

cues.en: rightmost numbers, the patch number, These are things that shouldn't affect anything. Just a bug fix.
cues.zh: 右边的数字，也就是补丁号，这些不应该影响任何东西。只是修 bug。

cues.en: The minor number, the three, is a minor additional release.
cues.zh: 次版本号，也就是那个 3，是一次小幅额外发布。

cues.en: We've added some new APIs,
cues.zh: 我们加了一些新 API，

cues.en: things that weren't present in the old thing, but nothing has changed. No one will be broken. And the major number bump is reserved for I made a change to an existing API,
cues.zh: 旧版本里没有的东西，但什么都没变。不会破坏任何人的代码。而主版本号提升则保留给“我改了现有 API”，

cues.en: your code won't build.
cues.zh: 你的代码会构建失败。

cues.en: So when you express
cues.zh: 所以当你表达

cues.en: dependence on a particular
cues.zh: 对某个特定

cues.en: version
cues.zh: 版本

cues.en: of one of your underlying libraries, libutil,
cues.zh: 你某个底层库 libutil 的依赖时，

cues.en: you say, I depend on one dot three or better.
cues.zh: 你会说，我依赖 1.3 或更高。

cues.en: And one dot three or better means it could be one dot four, it could be one dot five, can't be two dot o because
cues.zh: 而 1.3 或更高意味着可以是 1.4，可以是 1.5，但不能是 2.0，因为

cues.en: in that one to two switch,
cues.zh: 在那次 1 到 2 的切换中，

cues.en: you made a breaking change.
cues.zh: 你做了破坏性变更。

cues.en: Scare quotes.
cues.zh: 反讽引号。

cues.en: Implicit in the system is that you can tell the difference ahead of time between a change that breaks someone and a change that doesn't.
cues.zh: 这个体系隐含的前提是，你能提前区分一个变更会不会破坏别人。

cues.en: And it's actually sort of worse than this. Using an incompatible major version doesn't mean that things won't work,
cues.zh: 而且实际上还更糟。使用不兼容的主版本并不意味着东西一定不能用，

cues.en: it just means things might not work.
cues.zh: 只是意味着东西可能不能用。

cues.en: It is entirely possible that the major version got bumped because of API changes that you don't actually care about.
cues.zh: 完全有可能主版本被提升，是因为你根本不在意的 API 变更。

cues.en: That is, imagine that LibA doesn't depend on everything in Libutil,
cues.zh: 也就是说，想象 LibA 并不依赖 Libutil 里的所有东西，

cues.en: only one part of it.
cues.zh: 只依赖其中一部分。

cues.en: Changes unrelated to APIs in Libutil may not affect LibA in any meaningful way.
cues.zh: Libutil 中与 API 无关的变更，可能不会以任何有意义的方式影响 LibA。

cues.en: And yet, in a SemVer sense, we've revved LibUtil to V two,
cues.zh: 然而，从 SemVer 的意义上说，我们已经把 LibUtil 升到了 V2，

cues.en: and a new major version, because there was a incompatible
cues.zh: 一个新的主版本，因为有一个不兼容的

cues.en: API change.
cues.zh: API 变更。

cues.en: So in some instances, SemVer is over constraining,
cues.zh: 所以在某些情况下，SemVer 约束过强，

cues.en: Which, if you've ever had trouble installing something because of version incompatibilities,
cues.zh: 如果你曾经因为版本不兼容而装不上东西，

cues.en: is not a pleasant thought.
cues.zh: 这可不是什么愉快的想法。

cues.en: I think it has been a week since I had that annoyance,
cues.zh: 我想距离我上次遇到那种烦恼已经过去一周了，

cues.en: and I would give you better than even odds that if we just
cues.zh: 而且我敢说，概率超过一半，如果我们只是

cues.en: made it shut up and turned off all of the version checking,
cues.zh: 让它闭嘴，关掉所有版本检查，

cues.en: it would probably work.
cues.zh: 它很可能就能用。

cues.en: Very annoying.
cues.zh: 非常烦人。

cues.en: But, assuming
cues.zh: 但是，假设

cues.en: that you can identify what breaks your users, and assuming that you're okay with that slight over conservatism,
cues.zh: 你能识别出什么会破坏你的用户，并且假设你能接受那点过度保守，

cues.en: this does give us a standard way of identifying things that will work together.
cues.zh: 这确实给了我们一种标准方式，来识别哪些东西能一起工作。

cues.en: Note what SemVer doesn't say. This is not providing any form of proof that your dependencies
cues.zh: 注意 SemVer 没说什么。它并没有提供任何形式的证明，证明你的依赖

cues.en: can work out.
cues.zh: 能协调好。

cues.en: It is just saying that if there is a set of versions for your dependencies that satisfies all stated constraints,
cues.zh: 它只是说，如果你的依赖存在一组满足所有已声明约束的版本，

cues.en: you can in theory find it.
cues.zh: 理论上你就能找到它。

cues.en: And of course, each version of all of your dependencies comes with its own requirements.
cues.zh: 当然，你的每个依赖的每个版本，都带着自己的要求。

cues.en: And it is especially important
cues.zh: 尤其重要的是

cues.en: to note that any dependency tree you see that fits on a slide is wildly simplified.
cues.zh: 要注意，任何能塞进一页幻灯片的依赖树，都被极度简化了。

cues.en: And that popular dependencies are very popular.
cues.zh: 而且，流行的依赖非常流行。

cues.en: And that diamonds form at many levels and scales.
cues.zh: 而且，菱形依赖会在许多层级和规模上形成。

cues.en: And as your dependency graph grows,
cues.zh: 而当你的依赖图增长时，

cues.en: it grows quadratically.
cues.zh: 它会以二次方速度增长。

cues.en: That is how graphs grow.
cues.zh: 图就是这样增长的。

cues.en: Only a linear fraction of your dependency graph is under your control.
cues.zh: 你的依赖图中只有线性的一小部分在你控制之下。

cues.en: Box. You get to pick the things that are directly
cues.zh: 方框。你能选择那些你直接

cues.en: depended upon by you.
cues.zh: 依赖的东西。

cues.en: You do not necessarily have control over the dependencies of everything else in your graph.
cues.zh: 你未必能控制图中其他所有东西的依赖。

cues.en: Do the math.
cues.zh: 算算就知道了。

cues.en: The chances that SemVer and its potential slight over constraining leaves you with an unsatisfiable
cues.zh: SemVer 及其潜在的轻微过度约束，会让你落到一个无法满足的

cues.en: dependency tree grows quadratically.
cues.zh: 依赖树；这种概率会二次方增长。

cues.en: We are doing better and better in the open source world of making things shareable,
cues.zh: 在开源世界里，我们越来越擅长让东西可共享，

cues.en: and we are heading to disaster.
cues.zh: 而我们正走向灾难。

cues.en: Why do we use SemVer?
cues.zh: 为什么我们用 SemVer？

cues.en: It is a compromise position between nothing ever changes and there is no stability promise.
cues.zh: 它是在“永远什么都不变”和“没有任何稳定性承诺”之间的折中。

cues.en: There is nothing about this that is necessary,
cues.zh: 这没有任何必然性，

cues.en: nor is it in any way sufficient.
cues.zh: 也绝谈不上充分。

cues.en: As your dependency graph expands,
cues.zh: 随着你的依赖图扩大，

cues.en: dependence on semver is equivalent to I sure hope that major version bumps in my graph happen sufficiently and frequently that this all works out.
cues.zh: 依赖 SemVer 就等于说：我真心希望我图里的大版本升级发生得足够多、足够频繁，好让这一切都能成立。

cues.en: It's a hope and a prayer.
cues.zh: 这就是指望和祈祷。

cues.en: What's the difference between a patch release and a major version? It gets worse.
cues.zh: 补丁版本和大版本有什么区别？更糟的是，

cues.en: That is, what guarantee are you giving when you bump from one three seventeen to one three eighteen that you aren't giving when you go to two o o?
cues.zh: 也就是说，当你从 1.3.17 升到 1.3.18 时，你给出了什么保证，而升到 2.0.0 时却没有给？

cues.en: That is,
cues.zh: 也就是说，

cues.en: put it another way, what constitutes a breaking change?
cues.zh: 换个说法，什么才算破坏性变更？

cues.en: And because I've done quite a bit to change and update Google's code base over the years, I can answer this quite confidently.
cues.zh: 因为这些年我为修改和更新 Google 的代码库做了不少事，我可以很有把握地回答。

cues.en: Almost everything.
cues.zh: 几乎一切。

cues.en: Breaking change ness is not binary.
cues.zh: 破坏性变更程度不是二元的。

cues.en: Give it a little bit of time to to do a profile for us. Let's see exactly what it is that's making this faster or slower based on the different inputs. I mean, you can really gain a lot of insight by actually looking at the profile like this.
cues.zh: 稍等片刻让它跑完分析。我们来看看在不同输入下，究竟是什么导致了变快或变慢。我的意思是，直接观察这样的分析结果，真的能带来很多启发。

cues.en: I worked at Sesame Street. I got brought on to be a writer's assistant on a show called Sesame Street English,
cues.zh: 我曾在 Sesame Street 工作过。当时我加入了一个叫 Sesame Street English 的节目当编剧助理，

cues.en: which was to teach English to kids in China and Japan.
cues.zh: 这个节目旨在教中国和日本的孩子学英语。

cues.en: It seems very simple, the shows that they put together, but it's it's actually really hard to design a show that is not only for young kids, but also the parents.
cues.zh: 他们做出来的节目看似简单，但要设计出一个不仅面向儿童、还能吸引家长的节目，实际上非常难。

cues.en: Confession like this is therapeutic. I hope you all get something out of this, but if you don't, the therapy will have been good for me, so thank you.
cues.zh: 这样的坦白很有疗愈效果。希望大家能从中有所收获，但即使没有，这次倾诉对我自己来说也是一种疗愈，谢谢大家。

cues.en: Seven years ago, I was working...
cues.zh: 七年前，我还在……

cues.en: I wasn't working at Google. I was... For my previous employer, which was large multinational investment bank. I had what was up to that point the worst day of my career. And then came the anger.
cues.zh: 那时我还没在 Google 工作。我在……上一家公司，是一家大型跨国投资银行。那天是我职业生涯截至当时最糟糕的一天。随之而来的便是愤怒。

cues.en: Anger at ourselves because we knew we were responsible
cues.zh: 对我们自己的愤怒，因为我们知道自己负有责任——

cues.en: for America's first space disaster.
cues.zh: 要对美国的第一起航天灾难负责。

cues.en: We wrote two more words into our vocabulary as mission controllers,
cues.zh: 作为飞行任务控制人员，我们在自己的字典里又添了两个词：

cues.en: tough and competent. Tough meaning we will never again shirk from our responsibilities because we are forever accountable for what we do. Competent will never again take anything for granted.
cues.zh: 坚韧（tough）与胜任（competent）。坚韧意味着我们绝不再推卸责任，因为我们永远要对自己的所作所为负责；胜任意味着我们绝不再把任何事视为理所当然。

cues.en: We will never stop learning. From now on, the teams and mission control will be perfect because as a team, we must never fail. One other thing.
cues.zh: 我们将永不停止学习。从现在起，任务控制团队必须做到完美，因为作为一个团队，我们绝不能失败。还有一件事。

cues.en: We're all in a very fortunate position.
cues.zh: 我们都处在一个非常幸运的位置。

cues.en: We've been very lucky in our lives and so forth.
cues.zh: 我们在生活中一直都非常走运，诸如此类。

cues.en: And I think as part of the mission, it's also good sometimes
cues.zh: 我认为作为使命的一部分，有时也应该

cues.en: to take that fortune and
cues.zh: 利用这份幸运，

cues.en: give back.
cues.zh: 去回馈社会。

cues.en: To make sure that we take this platform and use it towards worthy causes.
cues.zh: 去确保我们能利用这个平台，投入到崇高的事业中去。

cues.en: That's good karma.
cues.zh: 这是在积累善缘。

cues.en: That's good stuff in the universe. We understand that your event will have needs that are specific to your organization.
cues.zh: 这是世间的美好事物。我们理解，贵方的活动会有契合贵组织的特定需求。

cues.en: Please email or call us directly to discuss your particular event. We look forward to discussing your goals and helping make your event a success.
cues.zh: 请直接发送邮件或致电我们沟通具体的活动细节。我们期待与您探讨活动目标，并协助您的活动取得圆满成功。
